PH / LESSON 04 CONTINUATION MODEL

DON'T CHASE
THE MOVE.
READ THE INVITE.

A continuation is not “price is moving, so enter.” It is a higher-timeframe draw, a completed internal objective, and a failed reaction that tells you delivery is not finished.

START THE LESSON ↓
THE CORE PRINCIPLE / 01
“There has to be something left for price to go take.”

DRAW FIRST. SETUP SECOND. EXECUTION LAST.

HTF DRAW→OBJECTIVE MET→REACTION→DISRESPECT→CONTINUATION

THE FRAMEWORK

LOGIC BEFORE
LOW TIME FRAME.

Every continuation begins with one question: where is price being drawn, and why is that draw still valid? A clean one-minute setup cannot create a higher-timeframe draw that does not exist.

CONTINUATION HAS A REASON.

Continuation does not mean entering anywhere in the direction price is flowing. It means the higher-timeframe and lower-timeframe stories agree, and there is still a logical objective for price to reach.

NO DRAW, NO TRADE.

If price has already taken the available highs or lows, stop looking for continuation in that direction. Displacement, SMT, or a clean reversal sequence cannot replace a missing draw.

INTERNAL VS. EXTERNAL.

An internal high, low, SIBI, or displacement candle may create a reaction on the way to the main external draw. Treat that reaction as a possible rebalance or manipulation, not an automatic reversal.

LET THE OBJECTIVE REACT.

Never enter simply because price touched the objective. Wait for its reaction, then wait for the reaction to be disrespected. The same execution may still be available minutes later with far better confirmation.

THE VALID CONTINUATION

THE DRAW IS STILL OPEN.

HTF narrative and intraday delivery agree. Price has taken an internal objective, but the main external objective remains untouched.

  • Clear directional draw
  • Speed through internals
  • Room to the main objective

THE FORCED CONTINUATION

NOTHING LEFT TO TAKE.

Once the objective is complete, momentum alone is not trade logic. Do not manufacture a target because displacement looks good.

  • Nearby draws already taken
  • Entering from FOMO
  • Target chosen after entry

AFTER AN OBJECTIVE IS TAKEN

WAIT FOR PRICE
TO SHOW ITS HAND.

The first touch of an internal high, low, displacement candle, or liquidity pool is not the entry. Let the objective produce a reaction. Then wait for price to disrespect that reaction.

01

OBJECTIVE MET

Price reaches an internal draw on the way to the external target.

02

REACTION

Let the pullback or manipulation invite the other side.

03

DISRESPECT

The reversal cannot sustain and price resumes with intent.

04

EXECUTION

Define invalidation beyond the rebalance and target the open draw.

EXECUTION NOTES FROM THE LESSON

WHAT YOU ARE
ACTUALLY WAITING FOR.

At every objective—an internal high or low, a SIBI, a displacement candle, or external liquidity—price is allowed to react. Your edge is not predicting that first reaction. Your edge is recognizing when it cannot hold.

MANIPULATION.

Price may sweep a nearby low on a bullish day or a nearby high on a bearish day, creating the appearance of reversal. If the main draw remains open, this can be the invitation that creates your continuation entry.

REBALANCE, THEN DISRESPECT.

Let price revisit the displacement leg. When it rebalances and then refuses to trade back through it, the rejection shows that delivery toward the main draw is resuming.

SOUP SEQUENCE FAILURE.

Three candles can appear to deliver away from an objective. Do not blindly enter the fourth. Wait for a rebalance and the disrespect of that rebalance; that is what turns context into an execution.

VOLATILITY CHANGES THE SHAPE.

Near the open, price may manipulate and deliver almost immediately. The sequence can be fast, but the rule does not change: identify the draw, read the reaction, and let candle closure confirm the failure.

TURTLE MODEL FAILED

THE REVERSAL
CAN'T CLOSE.

On a bullish day with a higher-timeframe draw above, a bearish Turtle Model is expected to fail. If the confirming bearish candle never closes, sellers have been invited—but not rewarded.

THE READ

The failure to close bearish is information. Expect the SMT and failed reversal structure to be taken as price continues higher.

  • 01 Bullish HTF narrative
  • 02 External draw above
  • 03 Bearish close fails
  • 04 Reclaim confirms

SOUP SEQUENCE FAILED

THE PULLBACK
IS THE INVITE.

This often forms at an internal draw while price is delivering toward the main external draw. In strong bullish delivery, a sudden pullback can be manipulation—not a new bearish narrative.

US VS. THE MARKET

The market invites sellers, uses their stops as fuel, and continues toward the objective. Wait for the invite to fail, then trade the move that stops them.

LIVE CASE STUDY / BEARISH CONTINUATION

THE MOVE THAT
TRAPS THE CROWD.

HTF narrative was bearish. The open manipulated higher, rebalanced a four-hour SIBI, then began delivering toward the external draw below. NQ and ES were moving down with speed and efficiency when price suddenly flipped higher.

01 / CONTEXT

NO MAJOR DRAW WAS TAKEN.

Neither NQ nor ES reached a meaningful objective before the bullish flip. With the bearish external draw still open, the move higher had the profile of manipulation—not a new narrative.

02 / THE INVITE

BUYERS SEE A REVERSAL.

The sudden rally invites breakout buyers and keeps traders married to longs from the opening manipulation. Their participation builds liquidity for continuation lower.

03 / CONFIRMATION

THE CANDLE FAILS AT THE 9 EMA.

In real time, the candle looked like bullish displacement. At closure, it failed to hold above the 9 EMA. That failure preserved the bearish continuation idea.

THE DISCIPLINE

Wait for candle closure. Intrabar movement creates urgency; the close reveals whether price actually held.

THE MARKET OFTEN DELIVERS IN THE DIRECTION THAT TRAPS THE MOST PARTICIPANTS.

LIVE CASE STUDY / BULLISH CONTINUATION

BEARISH SMT.
NO BEARISH EFFECT.

NQ was leading ES and took an internal high while major higher-timeframe draws remained above. That relative high created bearish SMT—but the daily narrative was bullish, and the divergence failed to produce meaningful bearish delivery.

01 / NARRATIVE

THE DAY IS BULLISH.

NQ and ES still have major higher-timeframe objectives above. The internal high is not the final destination; it is one draw on the path to the larger draw.

02 / SMT

NQ LEADS ES.

NQ takes the internal high while ES does not, creating bearish SMT. The divergence warns of a possible reaction, but it does not automatically create a short.

03 / REBALANCE

THE NEXT CANDLE REBALANCES.

Price revisits the displacement candle that took the draw. The pullback fills orders, but it does not create sustained bearish displacement or change the bullish narrative.

04 / CONTINUATION

THE SMT HAS NO EFFECT.

Price resumes higher. ES also shows no meaningful slowing and continues seeking its draws above, confirming that the bearish SMT was only an internal reaction.

THE TRAP

Eager traders see price pause after a strong move and try to top-tick the short. They trade the appearance of resistance instead of asking whether the SMT produced actual bearish delivery.

SMT IS INFORMATION. THE REACTION—OR LACK OF ONE—TELLS YOU WHETHER IT MATTERS.

PRIMARY CASE STUDY / BEARISH CONTINUATION

THE BUYER INVITE
GETS SOUPED.

The day is clearly bearish, with external liquidity and major higher-timeframe draws below. After taking an internal draw, price flips higher and invites buyers—but there is no logical reason for the market to reverse before reaching the real objectives.

01 / CONTEXT

CLEARLY BEARISH.

The higher-timeframe narrative and open external draws both point lower. The internal low is only one objective on the path to larger liquidity below.

02 / INVITE

PRICE FLIPS HIGHER.

The bounce invites retail buyers who read the one-minute movement instead of the day’s narrative. They FOMO into longs and mistake a pullback for reversal.

03 / SMT + EMA

NO BULLISH EFFECT.

NQ remains lower than ES, creating bullish SMT, but price still cannot deliver higher. Attempts to rally reject beneath the 9 EMA, confirming continued weakness.

04 / DELIVERY

SOUP THE BUYERS.

When the invitation fails, the buyers become liquidity. We trade the move that stops them out and continues toward the external and higher-timeframe draws below.

THE DECISION

Do not reverse the narrative because price bounced after an internal draw. Ask whether the reaction changed delivery. Here, bullish SMT and the move higher produced no sustained bullish displacement.

WHEN THE BULLISH SIGNAL CANNOT MOVE A BEARISH MARKET, ITS FAILURE IS THE CONTINUATION SIGNAL.

BEARISH CONTINUATION / HAMMER FAILURE

ONE BULLISH CANDLE
DOES NOT FLIP THE DAY.

The higher-timeframe narrative is bearish and the main draws remain lower. Price takes an internal objective and prints a bullish hammer, but there is no logical reason for the market to reverse at that location.

01 / NARRATIVE

DRAWS REMAIN LOWER.

The bearish day and open HTF objectives define the expected direction before the hammer ever forms.

02 / REACTION

THE HAMMER INVITES BUYERS.

After the internal is taken, the long lower wick looks like rejection. Eager traders interpret one candle as the start of a full reversal.

03 / CONFIRMATION

THE NEXT CANDLE IS BEARISH.

The market immediately fails to build on the hammer. The bearish close confirms that the reaction did not change delivery.

04 / EXECUTION

TRADE THE FAILED INVITE.

Enter with the bearish narrative, using the failed hammer structure for invalidation and the lower external draw for the objective.

THE READ

A candle pattern is not a narrative. When a bullish hammer forms inside a clearly bearish delivery and receives immediate bearish follow-through, the buyers it invited are likely about to lose.

LET THE NEXT CANDLE TELL YOU WHETHER THE HAMMER CREATED REVERSAL OR ONLY CREATED LIQUIDITY.

BEARISH CONTINUATION / SIBI REBALANCE

THE PULLBACK
RESPECTS CE.

The bearish narrative and higher-timeframe draw remain lower. After an internal objective is taken, price flips upward to rebalance the displacement leg—but the pullback enters the SIBI only to consequent encroachment and respects it.

01 / NARRATIVE

THE DRAW IS LOWER.

The day remains bearish and the larger objective below is still open. Taking an internal draw does not complete the higher-timeframe delivery.

02 / INVITE

THE INTERNAL CREATES A FLIP.

Price reacts upward after the internal is taken. Eager traders read the bounce as reversal and FOMO into longs against the day’s narrative.

03 / REBALANCE

SIBI TO CE.

The pullback rebalances the bearish displacement by entering the SIBI to consequent encroachment. Price respects CE instead of displacing through the imbalance.

04 / EXECUTION

DELIVERY RESUMES.

The respected SIBI confirms that the move higher was a rebalance and buyer invite. We can trade their stop-out toward the HTF draw below.

THE DISTINCTION

A pullback into an imbalance is not automatically reversal. If price only rebalances to CE, respects the SIBI, and the external draw remains open, the original delivery is still in control.

THE REBALANCE GIVES PRICE A REASON TO CONTINUE—AND GIVES THE INVITED BUYERS A PLACE TO BE WRONG.
